review_notes: Melody judicial +1/high holds: three of her own statements point to pole_b (pamphlet 'safeguard our rights' and broad state-law protections [S1], 'State law is really the backbone of a lot of our rights' [S9], Kagan as a model for 'practical implications' [S10]), and the 'stay in its lane' remark [S12] plus the text-based Hauk opinion [S7] are real counterweight that correctly keeps her off +2. Her precedent standard ('legally incorrect and presently harmful') is Washington's standard test, which Edwards also states, so it was rightly not used as evidence. Edwards judicial -2/high holds: repeated explicit as-written statements across the pamphlet [S1], the June Q&A [S8] and the Seattle Times [S6]. His preference for the I-2066 dissent, which would have upheld more of a voter measure, does not cut against restraint. One basis error: the quote 'You cannot inject your policy views' comes from the June Center Square Q&A [S8], not from 'October interviews'. The citation is right and the score stands. Experience scores are consistent with Angelis (-1, short-tenure appointed incumbent) and with Bloom (+2, a pure renewal pitch) versus Edwards (+1, outsider with a long litigation record). Safety is correctly omitted for both. Melody's only safety-adjacent item is the Seattle Times saying she is bringing public involvement into bail reform, with no stated position [S12]. Party endorsements are not used in any basis. Summary/highlight flags: Melody's summary says she frames state courts as 'the main protectors' of rights. Her own words are 'backbone of a lot of our rights' and 'must safeguard our rights', so 'main' slightly overstates and 'important protectors' would be closer. The race_blurb is consistent with the dossier. The contest dossier calls Edwards 'a Seattle tax attorney' [S5], while his dossier and the scoring summary say Bainbridge Island. The scoring file uses Bainbridge, which is fine.
